reviews.text: Respectful and professional treatment
Excellent treatment of my dog, they take great care of him.
The veterinarians were very honest with their diagnosis.

We are so grateful to Dr. Diana and Dr. Ivanna for treating our Golden Retriever. She had gastric problems, and other veterinarians couldn't figure out how to treat her, but SF Veterinary Hospital immediately knew what she needed and took excellent care of her.
Highly recommended.
I went there urgently and they rudely refused to see me. I needed an ultrasound and they couldn't do that either. I deeply regret turning around and leaving with such a bad impression.

Excellent service and doctors! I highly recommend Dr. Alondra Lugo from the night shift and Dr. Josué Vega. They are excellent doctors who treated my daughter Cleo very well, and she finally received a diagnosis after visiting many other places. 100% recommended! ❤️

I want to share our experience from Friday, August 7th, around 8:00 p.m.
We arrived with Catrina, our dog, who was bleeding from her paw after tearing off a nail. What bothered us most wasn't the wait, but the lack of empathy and attention from the reception staff. For about 25 minutes, we repeatedly asked when a doctor could see her, while my husband held Catrina in his arms and she continued to bleed. The response was simply, "I already told you, everyone is busy."

I want to especially thank the maintenance lady, who was kind enough to approach us, ask if we had been seen yet, and personally seek help. I also want to thank Dr. Laura Alejandra García Ramírez, who finally saw us with great kindness and patience.

However, I think it's important to point out that a situation like this requires sensitivity and a sense of urgency. Even during the consultation, the doctor had to leave several times because there were no gauze pads or scissors in the office.

Hopefully, this experience will lead to a review of care processes and, above all, a reminder that behind every patient is a worried family and a beloved animal that needs care. Empathy is also an essential part of veterinary care.

We had a bad experience before, but we gave her a second chance. A few days ago, I went with my girlfriend and my pet to the emergency room, and we were completely satisfied with Dr. Alondra's work. She was very attentive, explained everything, ordered the necessary tests, and told me what was wrong with my cat. She hospitalized him, and now he's home. She's an excellent doctor; I highly recommend her, but she's only available at night.
Not satisfied. The ultrasound machine wasn't working when I brought it in, and the diagnosis was incorrect. The response time by phone and message was very slow. I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT.
Completely professional, they explain things very well.

The veterinarians there are inexperienced. Priscila and Uriel treated my dog, gave her an injection, and returned her to me weaker and with a spasm. They tried to hide the damage by wrapping her in a blanket. I absolutely do not recommend this hospital.

Normally, San Francisco is my go-to hospital, but ever since someone called Magui, who was on the team, I do everything I can to avoid being seen by her. She's rude, bossy, and doesn't answer any of my questions. Terrible service and awful customer service.

Excellent service, my dog ​​Muzza had to undergo surgery and fortunately she has been recovering well. The interest and professionalism of the staff and Dr. Priscilla, who has been following up with her, is evident.

Avoid this veterinary clinic! Please read all the negative reviews so you can see what kind of place it is: they once caused irreversible damage to a dog that could have been prevented! Read the bad reviews; I'll share ours: we were so disappointed that I just want to prevent more people from going there.

We took our cat in for an emergency because he had a problem during the night, and it was the closest place with 24-hour service.

The veterinarian who saw us was rude and made unnecessary comments about how difficult our cat was to handle: he was a sick cat, in pain and scared; there was no need to mock him for being difficult to deal with!

They started treating our cat without informing us of the costs beforehand. When they told us he had to stay overnight and gave us the total amount to pay, we felt it was outrageous that they hadn't told us the cost of each service upfront so we could agree to it. We had to pay 3,400 pesos at that moment, when ideally they should have explained the cost from the beginning.

The poor service didn't end there. The place where they keep the animals smells bad and the atmosphere is hostile. The next day they were supposed to give us an update at 5 pm. At 2 pm we decided to call, and it was extremely difficult to get through; every time they were going to transfer us to the appropriate department, they hung up on us. After half an hour, we finally got through, and only after we asked did they tell us that our kitten was already over his problems. Where is the sensitivity to communicate with people and let them know as soon as their ailment is resolved? Zero sensitivity on their part!

When we picked him up, they gave us the medication he needed, again without providing a detailed breakdown of the cost of each medicine: that added another 1,800 pesos.

Oh! And I already know how the vet's account will respond to my review, since every time someone comments on the poor service they received, they respond passive-aggressively, justifying each of their mistakes. At least have the decency to admit your errors and accept constructive criticism. If you don't love animals and lack the sensitivity to treat them as they deserve and to show the same respect and sensitivity to the people who entrust you with the health and lives of our pets, DON'T OWN A VETERINARY CLINIC AND DON'T PROFIT FROM PEOPLE'S NEEDS.

We will never take our pets here again, and rest assured we will spread the word so more people know about this terrible place. They take advantage of being open 24 hours to provide care however they please, because obviously, in the face of any danger, it's non-negotiable, and people end up in places like this just so their pets get quick attention.

And to the vet's account: spare us the passive-aggressive comments trying to wash your hands of your terrible service—it only makes you look worse! No matter how much you try to justify your awful practices, the negative reviews speak for themselves!

I took my dog ​​to a dermatologist after visiting five other veterinarians, and the doctor quickly understood what I was telling him. My dog ​​has a condition common to one of the breeds she's a mix of, and he treated her according to one of the possible approaches I had already researched so I could advocate for her, all in a single appointment.

At a follow-up visit, I mentioned a lump on her mammary gland, and he immediately called Dr. Uriel at the hospital, who took the time to explain what we were seeing and what the possible next steps were. I followed his recommendation, and although I had read reviews about a lack of communication (and, obviously, considering that I'm the one who has to advocate for my dog), we continued with her x-rays, her ultrasound, and finally, I scheduled her surgery.

Everyone at the hospital was incredibly kind. I don't know how to explain that I saw the peace in their eyes, and I'd like to think I also saw their understanding, because I did cry. They trusted each other as a team, and that made me trust them (the staff who greeted me every time I went to reception had complete confidence in Dr. Uriel and the anesthesiologist).

My dog ​​came out perfectly and is healing super fast. It was worth coming all the way from Tlaxcala.

Thank you so much!
One of the best in Guadalajara, excellent service, the Dogtores are very good.
Excellent service and good doctors
Very clean. Trained staff. Reasonable prices.
They took care of our kitten and treated him wonderfully; he's already recovered and full of energy again 💕 …
Their areas always smell bad, and there's dried urine in the reception area that they don't clean. It makes me not feel comfortable going there.

Our little one was hospitalized for over 7 days. He was attacked by a Pitbull, so he had to undergo surgery, and during his hospital stay, he received excellent care. Dr. Penelope and the entire team were fantastic. The treatment is spectacular. They give the little ones all the respect and love they deserve. The grooming service was also superb! My Yorkies looked like teddy bears. So, highly recommended.

Today, April 6th, I'm sharing my experience with this clinic again. Unfortunately, this time it's "NOT POSITIVE"—quite the opposite. I'm very upset about the terrible diagnosis they gave us for Blacky. "Dr. Gustavo," who in my opinion should be in another profession, gave us a diagnosis based on the information he had in the little guy's file. However, thanks to taking him to a traumatologist to validate what he had told me, it turned out that it was none of that, but rather he tested positive for ehrlichiosis, an enlarged spleen, a heart murmur, and we had to hospitalize him urgently.

I want to express my sincerest gratitude to the entire SF team for the excellent care Cheto received. Thanks to Dr. Daphne's timely attention, who took the time to thoroughly investigate a previous surgery that hadn't gone well, they were able to act correctly and promptly.

I also thank Dr. Juan, who performed the surgery with great professionalism, as well as all the follow-up appointments and consultations that have been key to Cheto's recovery.
All the staff are very kind, including Dr. Diana, who has also provided excellent care for our other two dogs.
It's a place where they truly care about their patients and provide humane and warm treatment to their owners. Even the facilities are always spotless. Thank you so much for everything!

Today I had a very bad experience at the San Francisco (SF) Veterinary Clinic, and I was quite disappointed.

On Thursday, I took in a kitten I rescued because he was very weak, infected, and malnourished. I admitted him so he could receive care and treatment. That day, I paid $2,800 for a complete blood count and a fecal exam, and I also left a 50% deposit.

Today, I went to pick him up around 5:00 pm. Fortunately, the kitten seemed a little more stable, and in terms of appearance, he's fine, and the amount they charged me wasn't what I expected (well, they still haven't given me the fecal exam results). However, the problem started as soon as I arrived: the staff didn't have clear information about my case. They asked me if I had already paid in full, when in reality, I had already left a deposit. After clarifying this, they charged me the remaining balance.

When I asked about the tests, they initially told me there was nothing on record. After checking, they finally found them. When I asked about the kitten's condition, they told me they didn't know, as they hadn't received any instructions or notes from the veterinarian who treated him. They told me to come back later to speak directly with the doctor.

Even when I asked about the necessary care, the answer was the same: they couldn't tell me anything because there was no information. Regarding the fecal sample, they said it wasn't recorded in the system, and that if it had been taken, the results would arrive in a few days.

In short, I encountered a complete lack of organization and communication. There was no clarity in the follow-up of the case, the treatments administered, or the tests performed. I left with the feeling that, despite having paid for the care and boarding, I didn't receive the information or service I expected.
How can you believe there's no medical record and that doctors don't communicate patient status?

Fortunately, I took the kitten to another veterinarian to ensure he receives the proper care.
Don't take them there, they charge a fortune and have terrible service and attention. BEWARE

I went directly to the vet to ask for information about scheduling an appointment for my dog ​​because of a problem with his teeth, and they gave me the vet dentist's card to make the appointment directly. I contacted the vet via message, but he never scheduled my appointment. It seems he's not interested in taking on new patients.

That's my experience.

Terrible service.
The staff doesn't want to work. I went to buy a bag of croquettes, and someone came out to tell me they couldn't serve me or sell them to me "because they might get in trouble." How can you get in trouble for selling in a place that's designed for selling and serving customers?
It's unacceptable that they employ people like that.

Dr. Uriel, the oncologist, is terrible; I absolutely do not recommend him. He operated on my dog ​​to remove a very small lump in her mammary gland in October, and now, at the beginning of March, she is dying. Her entire body is covered in cancer. I regret having her operated on without any prior testing beyond a simple x-ray taken by the doctor, whose fees, by the way, were quite high. Yes, I am writing with great sorrow, but I don't think things were handled right. He doesn't even interpret the pathology reports; he sends you to another specialist and doesn't follow up. He doesn't care if the cancer might return or order any tests after the surgery. In short, I know this won't cure my dog.

Dr. Federico, the dentist, is a great doctor and an excellent person. The procedure he performed on her teeth was excellent.

I made an appointment to bathe my dog ​​and took him at 9:00 a.m. At 3:30 p.m., I called to confirm if he was ready and they said yes, I could pick him up.

When I arrived, they charged me before handing him over. After waiting about 20 minutes, the receptionist came out to tell me there had been a mix-up and that they had bathed another dog with the same name as mine. In other words, six and a half hours had passed since I dropped him off, and I didn't even know what area my pet had been taken to. There was no indication of grooming, boarding, nothing; he was just in a cage.

I asked which area they had him in if he wasn't in grooming, and they just told me it was the fault of the morning shift. They offered to let me come back later to have him bathed or leave him overnight at boarding and pick him up the next day.

I asked to see where my dog ​​was at that moment (if he was in a cage or what his condition was) and they said yes, but that first they had to "notify" and "fix the place where he was." This made me very suspicious, since they didn't allow me to see him immediately.

I decided to have him returned without the service. Furthermore, they charged me before returning him and I had to request a refund to my card; even though they canceled the process, it took a while for the money to appear.

Terrible service, lack of oversight, and zero transparency. I would never entrust my pet to them again.
They are excellent, highly trained, and have a very humane approach to dogs. In dentistry and dermatology, they are the best! 🤩🐕😀 …

Excellent rabbit hospital! They treated my bunny and followed up with her until the end of her treatment. Very affordable prices and the veterinarians are very professional and caring. Highly recommended!

There are good veterinarians, but they have a BIG PROBLEM: internal communication between vets and external communication with clients.

My respects to Dr. Federico, the dentist, and Dr. Daphne.

But they have several very significant problems:

1- Communication via WhatsApp is slow, which hinders follow-ups with difficult dogs. They also have about three WhatsApp numbers and can't agree on which one to use.

2- Phone calls are also difficult; sometimes they don't connect.

3- When it comes to delivering tests that they DO charge for, they take a very long time, or sometimes they forget to give them to you. FOR EXAMPLE, they owe me a stool sample from a WEEK AGO. My dog ​​has even passed away, and they still haven't given it to me. Another ultrasound I needed took about three weeks, or almost a month.

4- I was once told that a swab had been taken from my dog ​​that an external oncologist needed to review, and they told me it had been successfully sent to him. Later, I asked the external oncologist if it was true that it had been sent to him, and he said no. He even told me that "they're secretive about what they do."

I REPEAT, they have some good veterinarians, but they make mistakes, contradict themselves, or lack follow-up, which is obviously due to communication problems.

In an emergency, it's somewhat helpful, but it's best to go for a consultation first to find out what's wrong with your dog and be very clear with them.
They promised to deliver it bathed, but they delivered it to me very, VERY dirty.

Dr. Gustavo Ayala gave my rabbit (Oregano) truly EXCEPTIONAL care!!!
Both his treatment and professionalism are truly commendable. I am very grateful for how well he cared for my Oregano.

After visiting several veterinary hospitals with some biased diagnostics by money, here is always my second and more accurate opinion, so that is what we decided to always is possible bring out pets here.

They didn't tell me my dog ​​wasn't eating. She was there for four days and only ate enough for two, and then came back with diarrhea. According to them, everything was fine. They told me bathing was included, but they didn't do it. And finally, they didn't tell me about the extra cost for medication at the boarding facility. Be careful because they're great at taking your money, but terrible at providing good care.

Dr. Juan Pablo, a surgeon, does excellent work in the orthopedic department. He operated on my dog ​​because he had a torn ligament in his knee, and the surgery was a success, as was his recovery. He is incredibly attentive and always speaks honestly, explaining all possible scenarios from the beginning. He explains everything in detail so you understand clinical terminology and the step-by-step process, as well as providing preventative measures for the future. The hospital also offers excellent service; they take great care of the animals, and the attention is good.

I've been taking my cats there for over 10 years, and I firmly believe that healthcare isn't free. However, I disagree with undisclosed charges when you bring family members for treatment. The initial consultation was supposed to be free, and subsequent checkups were free. They charged for the first consultation and then $300 for the checkup, which is fine, but after that, since the attending veterinarian was off (I assume) for his day off, they charged me from zero because it was a new doctor at the same clinic. I wasn't notified, and they performed two tests, of which I only agreed to one—specifically, the more expensive one. The care has been good, but I don't think the lack of communication regarding the charges is appropriate.

I appreciate the care my pets receive; they are always dedicated and kind. It gives me peace of mind to know they offer 24-hour service, as it's very distressing for me to see my pets unwell and not be able to find anyone to help. I am extremely grateful for the dedication of Francisco, Lilian, and Jorge.

A hospital that heals with love, acts professionally, and truly cares for your pet.

I am so grateful for all the care Uriel and Brenda gave me. I can't thank them enough for everything they did for my fur babies.

I recommend them without hesitation.

We received excellent care.
Dr. Uriel Castro provided a clear diagnosis and gave us options to support my dog's treatment.
My dog ​​had a health issue, and we were out of town, yet they still provided us with care and advice.
It's a very comprehensive hospital. They perform the necessary tests for good care, not to harm the animals or extract more money. Their sole purpose is to provide the most accurate diagnosis! And they treat your pet with great care and kindness.
My family is grateful for all their attention.
Excellent doctors with excellent service; very kind people who helped our dogs after a fire. 100% recommended.

Excellent service, I highly recommend them. Dr. Dafne was very attentive and kind; she was able to save my Pomeranian puppy. At another hospital where he was hospitalized for six days, they had given me no hope, but with them, they discharged him in three days, and my puppy is much better. They saved my three-month-old puppy's life. The best hospital for your pets.

Today, July 21, 2025, I took my Lhasa Apso to the San Francisco Veterinary Hospital for a bath and haircut. When I picked her up, I noticed a small cut near her anus. The area was visibly red and irritated. When I asked about it, the staff indicated that it was possibly an injury caused by the clippers, but that “it wasn’t anything to worry about.”

A week passed, and that “minor wound” turned into a severe inflammation, with pus, intense redness, and a black spot in the center, indicating a possible abscess and necrosis. Alarmed by the worsening of the injury, I immediately took my dog ​​back to the clinic where she had received the service, requesting a checkup.

The reception staff directed me to a veterinarian, who, upon examining my dog, informed me that she had sacculitis (inflammation of the anal glands). However, he completely denied that this condition could have been caused or aggravated by the wound sustained during the haircut. Contrary to multiple veterinary sources and subsequent professional opinions, this veterinarian maintained that "sacculitis cannot be caused by an external injury."

Without anesthesia or pain medication, the veterinarian attempted to drain the inflammation by applying direct force to the swollen area. My dog ​​screamed in pain both times, which was heartbreaking to witness. No pain management protocol was followed, nor was there any sensitivity or care shown in treating an already visibly inflamed and possibly infected area. Even at the end, he didn't apply Microdasin or any disinfectant solution; he simply took a dry paper towel and wiped it off.

After this procedure, the veterinarian tried to charge me for the consultation. I refused, arguing that I was requesting a check-up for a wound inflicted at his own establishment, and that it was his ethical and professional responsibility to assess the damage at no additional cost. To this, the doctor responded that the grooming salon and the veterinary clinic were “completely separate areas,” despite being located in the same building, under the same name, and without this distinction being communicated to the client beforehand.

When I asked for his full name to file a complaint, he refused to provide it. Neither the assistant present nor the receptionist, who observed the treatment and negligence without intervening, provided it. The doctor's attitude was cold, indifferent, and inhumane, and he made it clear that they would not be responsible for any damage caused during the grooming service.

Later, I took my dog ​​to a second veterinary clinic, where they confirmed that it is indeed possible for a poorly treated wound or one caused during shaving to develop into sacculitis or even an abscess. This second veterinarian explained that in cases like my dog's, anesthesia should be used to avoid extreme pain, and he performed the drainage procedure professionally, taking all necessary hygienic and medical precautions.

According to the sources consulted and the opinion of specialists, it became clear that the original injury could have triggered the subsequent complication, and that the treatment at the first clinic was negligent and inhumane.

For all the above reasons, I am making this complaint public to warn other pet owners about the risks of going to the San Francisco Veterinary Clinic, where the staff has demonstrated a lack of ethics, sensitivity, and professional responsibility in a situation they clearly created themselves.

I will never again entrust my dog's health to a place that prioritizes profit over animal welfare and where they refuse to take responsibility for their actions. My dog ​​didn't deserve to go through that pain, nor did I deserve to be treated with contempt and evasiveness. For now, I am filing this complaint while I pursue legal action.

I've attached two photos of her wound. It wasn't as swollen or as large in these photos because she had already taken it to another doctor.

It's been quite an ordeal finding the right doctors; after learning my dog ​​has cancer, we began the search and thank God we fell into the best hands. He's just had his second surgery, and there's still a long road ahead, but having doctors like Uriel and Emelany gives us more hope :) They provided excellent treatment, explanations, and care for my fur baby. Thank you!

I'm not saying this with any malice, quite the opposite, but if you love your pet dearly, take them somewhere else. I live a couple of blocks from here, so over the years I've taken my dogs to the emergency room. More than half the time, they treated me reluctantly and charged an unjustifiable price, charging double what some places charge without any extra benefits compared to the cheaper ones. Although, to be honest, it's been about a year since my last visit there, so things might have changed, though I doubt it. I hope this helps those who love their pets as family members.

Hello! We brought our dogs to this clinic a year ago when they saved the life of my dog, Mostaza. She arrived almost dead and with very little chance of survival, but thanks to their quick attention, great empathy, excellent professional ethics, and outstanding service, she is alive today. We are grateful to Dr. Uriel and Dr. Lilian, who are among the best veterinarians we have ever met. They are all young but highly skilled and professional. Since then, several of our dogs have been their patients, and we have always received the best care. Currently, we have two dogs undergoing chemotherapy thanks to the professionalism of Dr. Melany.

Thanks to all these experiences, we wholeheartedly recommend the SF Veterinary Clinic and its doctors in Guadalajara. In fact, we travel from a town an hour and a half to two hours away because we are certain that they will heal our dogs here.

I called ahead of time because my dog has an eye issue that recently started. They gave me all the information I needed on the phone and when I got to the hospital they received me immediately and took me step by step explaining everything the why of it all with each test being done. Definitely recommend as they genuinely show they care for the well being of our companions
First-class service and care for pets. 👍👍👍 …
Zero customer service and terrible empathy for pets.

They have absolutely no interest in the animal's health. I took my dog ​​in with pneumonia, struggling to breathe. They kept her hospitalized for two days and returned her to me in worse condition, practically dying, with her paws covered in excrement. Gustavo Ayala, a so-called veterinarian, was the one who treated her. He ordered several tests, prescribed medication for only seven days, and then left her without treatment. Even though I asked if her pneumonia was under control, he said yes and that her breathing difficulties were due to her enlarged esophagus. He literally let her suffocate and just kept charging for the hospitalization without doing a single thing. At that hospital, they let animals die rather than help them. I wasted valuable time when another place could have saved her life. DO NOT RISK YOUR PETS.
Very good service, Dr. Sandra treated my dog ​​and her treatment, attention and dedication were excellent.

They're complete idiots. I left my dogs with them to be bathed on my wedding day, and at 2:48 pm they texted my husband saying their water had been cut off the day before, they ran out, and they wouldn't be able to bathe the dogs. At that point, there was no way we could fix it, and they just stood there doing nothing, notifying us. We took them before noon.

I apologize for not remembering the name of the veterinarian who treated my dog, but I am incredibly grateful because he saved my baby after a misdiagnosis at another vet. At the other clinic, they gave her so much medication that she ended up unconscious, refusing to eat or drink, and here it was the complete opposite. They also treated my cousin's dog here for skin problems a couple of years ago, and I have absolutely no complaints about them; quite the contrary.
I had an emergency with my dog ​​in the middle of the night, and honestly, the care at this hospital was excellent. …
Excellent service, very good doctors and specialists 😊 Thank you for taking care of our furry children ❣️ …
Excellent service, very well looked after
